overview.headline: Weight as gravitational force and its small decrease with altitude

keyPoints.point: Weight is the force from gravitational attraction on an object, distinct from aerodynamic lift and drag forces
keyPoints.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyPoints.point: Newton universal gravitation says gravitational force between particles depends on product of masses and square of distance
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force, F, between two particles equals a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles, m1 and m2

keyPoints.point: On the surface of the earth gravitational acceleration value is 9.8 meters per square second derived from Earth properties
keyPoints.quote: On the surface of the earth, its value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second.

keyPoints.point: Weight equals mass times gravitational acceleration and decreases with altitude as distance from Earth center increases
keyPoints.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.

keyTerms.gloss: force generated by gravitational attraction acting on an object with mass
keyTerms.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyTerms.gloss: field force that acts without needing physical contact between source and object
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyTerms.gloss: combined value formed from gravitational constant and Earth mass and radius
keyTerms.quote: to form the gravitational acceleration, g.

keyTerms.gloss: product quantity of particles that determines strength of gravitational attraction
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force, F, between two particles equals a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles, m1 and m2

keyTerms.gloss: distance height where weight decreases as distance from Earth center grows
keyTerms.quote: we would expect that the weight of an object would decrease with altitude.
